title: Tri-City Painting Alternative: Warranty & Upkeep
description: Comparing Tri-City Painting and Precision Paint Experts? What to ask about warranties, touch-up paint, and keeping a new finish looking good for years.
h1: Tri-City Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: The day the crew leaves is the start of a paint job's life, not the end. This guide covers the after-the-job questions worth asking any painter.

sections.h2: Compare what happens after the last coat
body: Tri-City Painting is one of the painting companies North Central Florida homeowners may be comparing with Precision Paint Experts. We will not characterize anyone else. This page looks at a part of every proposal that is easy to overlook while you are focused on price and start date: the close-out, the warranty, and the upkeep that keeps a finish looking right.
Two jobs can look identical on the last day and age very differently. What is promised in writing about the months and years afterward is a fair way to tell proposals apart.

Precision Paint Experts closes every job with a punch walk the client signs. Anything not right at that final walkthrough is fixed before the job is closed out. Ask any contractor how their close-out works, who attends, and whether you sign off in writing.

We would rather hear about a concern while the crew is still on site than after they have left, so the walkthrough is the moment to point out anything that looks uneven, missed, or different from what was agreed in the scope.

sections.h2: Reading a warranty side by side
body: There are usually two separate warranties on a paint job: the manufacturer's warranty on the product, and the contractor's warranty on the labor. They cover different failures. Ask each bidder:
bullets: Is there a written workmanship warranty, separate from the product warranty?
How long does it last on exterior versus interior work?
What kinds of failure does it cover, such as peeling or blistering?
How do I make a claim?

body: Our exterior projects carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. We also leave labelled touch-up paint, so a scuff on a hallway wall or a nick on a door can be matched in color and sheen without guessing.

Upkeep matters too. Washing off pollen and mildew before it sets in extends a finish; our articles on cleaning Florida pollen stains and restoring sun-faded paint cover what to watch for. When an exterior needs more than a rinse, our soft washing service can clean it without a full repaint. Our exterior care calendar lays out a simple year of maintenance.

A simple habit helps more than most people expect: walk around the house twice a year and look for peeling at the bottom of trim boards, gaps in caulk around windows and doors, and dark streaks on shaded walls. Catching those early means a small repair rather than a large one. Interior walls benefit from the same attention; wiping scuffs gently and touching up with the labelled paint keeps a room looking fresh between repaints. If you keep the touch-up cans indoors, away from heat in a garage, they will stay usable longer.
